replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: The closed-basin period comes from Anderson & Lewis’s Lake Ontario reconstruction. Their work places a hydrologically closed lowstand in the Ontario basin from roughly 12,300 to 8,300 years ago, when upper Great Lakes drainage was diverted through the North Bay/Ottawa route and bypassed Lake Ontario. Later work by Lewis and others uses the same reconstruction. It’s definitely one of the stranger parts of Lake Ontario’s post-glacial history.
